name: Simon van Gaal
bio:
Lab and campus impressions

I am a cognitive neuroscientist working at the Brain and Cognition department of the University of Amsterdam (associate professor) and head of the Conscious Brain lab together with Johannes Fahrenfort and Timo Stein.

In the lab we study the neural correlates of consciousness and the role of consciousness in cognitive control and decision-making using various imaging techniques (e.g., EEG, functional and structural MRI, MEG). Hopefully, this will eventually contribute to a better understanding of the neural mechanisms and function of consciousness.

©2019 by conscious brain lab.

name: Johannes Fahrenfort
bio:
Lab and campus impressions

I am a cognitive neuroscientist in the Cognitive Psychology section at the Free University Amsterdam, and a PI in the Conscious Brain Lab (UvA/VU) together with Simon van Gaal and Timo Stein.

In the Conscious Brain Lab we use EEG, fMRI and psychophysics to investigate consciousness, with special emphasis on the contribution of decision making (confidence, metacognition), perception, attention and working memory to conscious experience. My current line of research explores the impact of perceptual bias and criterion setting on putative correlates of conscious and unconscious processing. In addition, I am developing a new research line investigating the neural mechanisms at play when people attempt to control sensations and actions that are normally deemed automatic and cognitively impenetrable (such as pain and other sensory responses). I have special expertise in EEG, for which I have developed the ADAM toolbox that implements decoding and forward modeling of EEG data.

©2019 by conscious brain lab.

name: Timo Stein
bio:
Lab and campus impressions

Before joining the Brain and Cognition group at the Department of Psychology at the University of Amsterdam in 2016 I did a postdoc at University of Trento with Marius Peelen , and a PhD at Berlin School of Mind and Brain with Philipp Sterzer and John-Dylan Haynes . In ancient times I studied ( neuro-cognitive ) psychology in Mainz, Munich , and Princeton . I am currently co-PI in the Conscious Brain lab together with Johannes Fahrenfort and Simon van Gaal.

©2019 by conscious brain lab.

name: Ana-Maria Barosan
bio: I started my PhD at the Conscious Brain Lab in September 2024, supervised by Simon van Gaal and Timo Stein. During my PhD, we aim to investigate the neural mechanisms through which arousal influences perceptual decision-making, focusing on how arousal modulates our ability to perceive and make decisions based on sensory information. To achieve this, we will use neuroimaging techniques, including fMRI and EEG, alongside pharmacological studies. Our first project will incorporate fMRI, psychophysics, and pupillometry to explore these effects. Before my PhD, I completed a BSc in Psychology, followed by a Research Master’s (MSc) in Psychology, specializing in Brain & Cognition, at the University of Amsterdam.

name: Ivan Ivanchei
bio: I joined the Conscious Brain Lab in August 2024 with a Marie Curie project on probabilistic learning and awareness. My research investigates how people become aware of what they learn in probabilistic learning situations. I examine behavioral, metacognitive, and physiological indices of learning, focusing on what they reveal about awareness of acquired knowledge. Previously, my research focused on implicit learning, the interaction between conscious and unconscious processes, and the role of affective processes in cognition. I completed my PhD at St. Petersburg State University and held postdoctoral positions at Ghent University and Université libre de Bruxelles.

name: Lola Beerendonk
bio: I started my PhD at the Department of Psychology of the University of Amsterdam in January 2018. In my NWO funded PhD project, I will investigate the influence of cortical state and neuromodulation on conscious perception. To this end, I will combine EEG, pupillometry, behavioral manipulations, and pharmacological interventions. Hereby, I hope to elucidate the influence of fluctuations in endogenous activity on consciousness. Before starting my PhD, I studied Natural and Social Sciences (‘Bèta-Gamma’, BSc) and Brain and Cognitive Sciences (MSc) at the University of Amsterdam. During my first research internship at the Consciousness and Cognition Lab at the University of Cambridge, I studied the influence of wakefulness on cognitive control. I investigated the neural correlates of consciousness in a no-report paradigm during my second internship, which was supervised by Simon van Gaal.

name: Maartje de Jong
bio: I investigate the way our brain transforms incoming sensory information into a meaningful image of the outside world, with a focus on visual perception. I use different techniques, including magnetic resonance imaging, scalp and intracranial electro-encephalography and psychophysics. My research interests include optical illusions, perceptual learning, ambiguous images, binocular rivalry and face perception. My background is in cognitive neuroscience, biology and experimental psychology.

name: Margot Steijger
bio: I joined the Conscious Brain Lab in September 2023 as a PhD student under supervision of Simon van Gaal. During my ERC funded project, I will focus on feedback processes in the brain and their relation to conscious perception by manipulating the NMDA and GABA receptors. My research will combine EEG, fMRI, eye tracking, behavioural tasks and pharmacological interventions. Before I started my PhD I obtained a degree in Psychobiology (BSc) and a in Cognitive Neuroscience (Brain and Cognitive Sciences, MSc) at the University of Amsterdam. My first research project was in this lab where I investigated recurrent processing and metacognition with EEG. My next project was at the LUMC, with a focus on magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS). Finally, I did my last research project at the Consciousness and Cognition Lab at the University of Cambridge, studying the effect of alertness and attention on cognitive control.

name: Nicolás Sánchez-Fuenzalida
bio: Former PostDoc I did my PhD at the Conscious Brain Lab in October 2018 fully funded by the National Commission for Scientific and Technological Research (CONICYT-Chile) investigating the role of consciousness in decisional threshold changes combining behavioural and physiological methods. In September 2023 I started a Postdoc at the Free University Amsterdam on the Templeton Grant "a statistical framework for establishing unconscious cognition" with Johannes Fahrenfort. ​ I graduated in Psychology (BS) and Philosophy (MS) at the University Diego Portales. Before starting my PhD and PostDoc I worked as a research assistant at the Center of Social and Cognitive Neuroscience where I studied Bayesian reasoning and health information communication.

name: Sean van Mil
bio: I am a PhD candidate at the University of Amsterdam's Conscious Brain Lab, supported by an ERC consolidator grant under Simon van Gaal's supervision. My academic journey began with a Bachelor's in Psychobiology, followed by a Master's in Biomedical Sciences, both at the University of Amsterdam. My passion for cognitive research led me to the University of Cambridge, where I completed my second internship and worked as a research assistant alongside Tristan Bekinschtein, Simon van Gaal and Andres Canales-Johnson. Our focus was on decision-making and neural dynamics under varying levels of drowsiness, and I continue to collaborate with Simon and the lab on related projects. My current PhD research investigates how different arousal levels impact performance and conscious perception. I will employ behavioral manipulations, pupillometry, and neural and physiological measurements to shed light on this intriguing aspect of the conscious brain.

name: Vlada Aslanov
bio: I started my PhD at the Cognitive Psychology section of the Free University Amsterdam in November 2023 under supervision of Johannes Fahrenfort. I will investigate the neural underpinnings of phenomenological control: the ability to experience the world differently from normal perception by overriding highly automated instances of information processing. My first project investigates at what level of the cortical hierarchy one can interrupt automatic processing using post-hypnotic suggestions.
